claims.text: Adding significant levels of Al and Cr to a high-entropy alloy promotes formation of a protective oxide film during service.
The proposed HEA forms a continuous protective oxide film in situ.
The proposed HEA's oxide film is adherent.
The proposed HEA's oxide film is stable at high temperature.
The protective oxide film resists chemical attack.
The protective oxide film resists mechanical wear.
Resistance of the oxide film to chemical attack and mechanical wear mitigates the synergistic degradation caused by tribo-corrosion.
The optimized Al- and Cr-containing HEA will have slower degradation rates than conventional structural alloys under elevated-temperature tribo-corrosive conditions.
The optimized HEA will exhibit less material loss than conventional structural alloys under the stated conditions.
The optimized HEA will have greater durability than conventional structural alloys under the stated conditions.
Conventional structural alloys are prone to accelerated degradation because they provide inadequate protection against the combined effects of elevated temperature and tribo-corrosion.
The stability and performance of the protective oxide film depend on temperature, wear intensity, corrosive species, and alloy processing.
